title: Notes on Elliptic Curves I & II

definitions.statement: L(E, s) = prod_{p | Delta} (1 - a_p p^(-s))^(-1) * prod_{p nmid Delta} (1 - a_p p^(-s) + p^(1-2s))^(-1).
P(X) = prod_{p <= X, p nmid Delta} N_p / p where N_p = #E(F_p).
E(Q) is a finitely generated abelian group isomorphic to Z^r oplus E(Q)_tors.

theorems.label: Hasse's Theorem
theorems.statement: |a_p| <= 2 sqrt(p) for all primes of good reduction.

conjectures.label: Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer Rank Conjecture
conjectures.statement: ord_{s=1} L(E, s) = rank E(Q) = r.

open_gaps: Conjecture formulation was purely empirical based on EDSAC-2 computations on Mordell curves y^2 = x^3 - Dx.
Analytic continuation of L(E, s) to s=1 was unproven in 1965 (later established by Wiles et al. 1995-2001).
computational_handles: Frobenius point counting #E(F_p) via Legendre symbols in O(p log p).
Partial Euler product P(X) growth regression against log(log X).
2-descent for upper bounding Selmer rank Sel^(2)(E/Q).

citations.ref: Birch, B.J., Swinnerton-Dyer, H.P.F. (1965). Notes on Elliptic Curves (II), J. Reine Angew. Math., 218, 79-108. GDZ Göttingen Digital Library.
Wiles, A. (2000). The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture - Official Clay Mathematics Institute Problem Description.
